newsitem.title: MEXICO: Looking for rebels, Mexican police rough up senator.
newsitem.headline: Looking for rebels, Mexican police rough up senator.

text.p: A Mexican senator was mistaken for a member of a new guerrilla group over the weekend and roughed up by a group of undercover police, his political party said on Tuesday.

Sen. Felix Salgado, of the left-of-centre Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), was accosted on Sunday on a rural road in his home state of Guerrero by five undercover security agents, said PRD spokesman Julio Ulloa.

Salgado was punched and grabbed by the throat by one of the men, who accused the senator of belonging to the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR), a guerrilla group that first appeared in the area in late June.

The men, who wore federal police badges, then planted an AK-47 automatic rifle in Salgado's car as evidence he was a subversive, Ulloa said. After learning that Salgado was a federal senator, the men were very apologetic but ran away when the senator demanded to know who they were.
Ulloa said the PRD and other parties would demand an investigation into the incident during Wednesday's legislative session.
"How many innocent people are being arrested in Mexico as part of the government's attempt to capture guerrillas?" he asked.

After the EPR launched attacks on military and police posts in several states late last month, President Ernesto Zedillo branded them as terrorists and vowed to bring them to justice using "the full force of the state."
